# E098 -- British Museum Design Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Brand**: British Museum
- **Industry**: Cultural Institution / Museum
- **Year**: March 2012
- **Source file**: `6fa362af8e41806e8afc59070d1af121.pdf`
- **Pages reviewed**: 1-2, 3-7, 12-13
- **Total pages**: 28
- **Format**: A4 (595x842)

## Brand Strategy
- **Purpose**: "The British Museum exists to promote dialogue and understanding."
- Collection spans dawn of human history (2 million years ago) to present.
- Positioning: a place for debate, committed to allowing a wide public to re-examine cultural identities and explore interconnected human cultures.
- **Design philosophy**: "It is important that the design system itself becomes recognisable, not the individual elements."
- No sub-brands, no exhibition "personalities" -- single organization, shared outlook.

## Logo
- Adapted from the font Baskerville, referencing the Museum's founding period (1753).
- Logo is a copyrighted trademark of the Trustees of the British Museum.
- **Must never be recreated** by typing in text; only official graphic files.
- **Color**: black or white only.
- **Minimum size**: 25mm width (standard), 16mm (optically adjusted small version).
- **Single-line version**: minimum 50mm width; optically adjusted single-line at 28mm minimum.
- **Clear space**: measured by width of the "M" in "Museum."
- Stacked version is always preferred.
- Do not reverse out of pale colours or busy backgrounds.
- All uses must be approved by Marketing Department (logo@britishmuseum.org).

## Typography
- **Serif (designed work)**: Baskerville -- same period as the Museum's 1753 founding; provides gravitas and authority.
- **Sans serif (designed work)**: Berthold Akzidenz Grotesk Pro -- contemporary, modern feel. Weights: Light, Regular, Medium, Bold, Super (all with italic variants).
- **Non-designed work/web**: Arial.
- Font sizes should ideally be multiples of 3.
- Text ranged left or right, never centred (except in circle defacers).
- Sentence case; no all-uppercase, all-lowercase, or small caps.
- **Type hierarchy example** (on-site poster 508x762mm):
  - 84pt Akzidenz Grotesk Pro Medium (headlines)
  - 48pt Akzidenz Grotesk Pro Light (dates/subheads)
  - 24pt Akzidenz Grotesk Pro Regular (calls to action)
  - 18pt Akzidenz Grotesk Pro Regular (sponsor text)
  - 9pt Akzidenz Grotesk Pro Regular (credits)
  - 48pt Akzidenz Grotesk Pro Light in circle defacer

## Color
- **Marketing materials**: black/dark backgrounds for charging exhibitions; white/pale backgrounds for free/core activities.
- Neutral backgrounds allow object colors to stand out.
- One-off special events can use colored backgrounds (ephemeral nature).
- Two-color text system: default first color black/white (based on background), second color complements the object image.
- Designer flexibility: e.g., two shades of blue instead of black+blue is acceptable.

## Graphics
- **Nine-column grid system**: core structural device for all design.
- Logo can be positioned anywhere within the nine-column grid.
- Circle defacer for promotional elements (e.g., "Coming soon" circles).
- No designed sub-brands -- activity names written in text only.

## Photography
- Objects from the collection are the "most important element of the design."
- Choosing the right object is critical to design strength.
- Different objects distinguish different activities.
- **Strict rule**: text and logo must never be placed over objects -- "always respect and protect objects."

## Applications
- On-site posters (508x762mm) with detailed font hierarchy.
- Marketing materials with exhibition vs. free activity color coding.

## Tone of Voice
- Not covered as a dedicated section. The document is primarily visual/design-focused.
- Implied tone: authoritative, scholarly, accessible, respectful.

## Outliers
- **Object-first design philosophy**: the museum's collection objects ARE the brand -- no illustrations, no sub-brand graphics. The object is always the hero and must never be obscured.
- **Anti-sub-brand stance**: explicit rejection of designed sub-brands or exhibition "personalities." Everything operates under one unified visual system.
- **Logo derived from Baskerville font**: direct historical connection to the Museum's founding era (1753) -- the typeface IS the brand heritage.
- Four optically-adjusted logo versions at different sizes is unusually precise.
- Font licensing addressed explicitly -- external partners must purchase fonts themselves.
- Nine-column grid as the structural DNA with flexible logo placement is a distinctive approach (most guidelines fix logo position).
- 28 pages -- concise but remarkably well-articulated.

## Quality Score
4/5 -- A masterclass in restrained, object-centered institutional design guidelines. The philosophy of letting the design system (not individual elements) become recognizable is sophisticated. Precise grid system, multiple logo size variants, clear color coding logic. Deducted one point for lack of TOV section and limited digital guidance (2012 document).
